paragraphs: Dreambeans is an experimental app from Google Labs that will “proactively dream up personalized daily stories.” After previously requiring a subscription, Dreambeans is now available for free Google Accounts in the US to test.
Update 9/10: Google officially announced the broader availability today.

Original 8/28: Dreambeans is very much like a hyper-personalized Google Now or Discover feed. Like the Gemini app and AI Mode, it uses Google’s Personal Intelligence system to learn your interests by looking at your Gmail, Google Photos, Calendar, Workspace, Search history, and YouTube. During setup, you can choose which apps Dreambeans can access.
By combining all these unique signals, Dreambeans can proactively generate rich and highly customized daily visual stories.
The app suggests topics to explore, things to try, places to visit, and interesting events. New stories arrive every morning.

Instead of using stock imagery, each Dreambeans story is accompanied by Nano Banana 2-generated artwork that uses an illustrated style. For example, if Dreambeans recommends a hike, you might see yourself and a group of friends at that location.

Tapping on a story lets you see a longer description. In the same example, you’ll get trail details, specific places to stop, what to wear, and timing recommendations. Dreambeans will link to trail guide content on the web. There’s also an “Ask anything” chat experience to get more information.

You can leave feedback by tapping the heart or downvoting, while the chat interface allows you to provide more details. “Tune your feed” lets you tell Dreambeans what you “want more stories about” and what it should never show.
